It includes a real-time clock (RTC) for time-stamping, overflow detection, and a readout state machine. The design is an early work-in-progress test implementation and is the second Tiny Tapeout submission, improving on a previous 4-channel version. External hardware such as a logic analyzer is recommended for debugging.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Coline3003_top.review_notes: Removed rtc and fsm as primary tags; added counter, sensor-interface, instrumentation, and verilog.

ttihp25a/tt_um_DaDDS.summary: DaDDS is an 8-bit direct digital synthesizer intended as an RF transmitter supporting OOK and FSK modulation. It accepts UART commands and frequency selection inputs, and outputs an 8-bit DAC signal. The documentation references architecture, UART protocol, and application diagrams but provides little textual explanation, so the exact operation and external hardware requirements are not fully described. It is notable for targeting high-frequency RF synthesis with digital modulation in a single tile.
ttihp25a/tt_um_DaDDS.review_notes: Removed synthesizer (audio connotation) and added signal-generator for the DDS waveform generation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Electom_cla_4bits.summary: This design is a 4-bit carry look-ahead adder that computes the sum of two 4-bit inputs plus a carry-in. It provides sum and carry-out outputs and can be used as a building block for larger adders. The design was tested on an FPGA but has no silicon test report. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand its function.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Electom_cla_4bits.review_notes: Removed alu tag; the design is an adder, not an arithmetic logic unit.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Esteban_Oman_Mendoza_maze.summary: This project is a maze explorer game implemented in Verilog, where the player navigates a maze using three input buttons to move forward and select direction. The game state and direction are output on bidirectional pins, and the maze walls are displayed on five 7-segment displays. It requires external hardware: five 7-segment displays, current-limiting resistors, and wiring. The design is a simple interactive game.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Esteban_Oman_Mendoza_maze.review_notes: Removed education and fsm (unsupported); added maze, 7-segment, and display.

ttihp25a/tt_um_I2C.summary: This project implements I2C and SPI communication protocols in Verilog. It provides pins for I2C data and clock, SPI MISO, MOSI, and SCK, along with output enables. The documentation is minimal, stating only that it is a design of I2C and SPI protocols and that testing involves sending data with an enable clock. No external hardware is required, but the lack of detailed documentation limits understanding of the implementation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_I2C.review_notes: Removed unsupported education tag and added insufficient-doc given the very thin documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_JAC_EE_segdecode.summary: This design is an ASIC implementation of a university CPLD project that drives four multiplexed seven-segment displays and scans a multiplexed keypad. It uses a simple SPI protocol to receive commands for display data and keypad column selection, and it outputs keypad row data on MISO. The design requires external hardware including displays, a keypad, and an SPI master, and it must be clocked by the SPI clock. Silicon testing showed it functional up to 3.7 MHz, but auto-clocking must be disabled.
ttihp25a/tt_um_JAC_EE_segdecode.review_notes: Tags and summary are supported; no changes needed.

ttihp25a/tt_um_JesusMinguillon_freqSweep.summary: This project implements a clock frequency sweeper that divides the input clock by 2 every 15 cycles, cycling from 1/2 to 1/16 of the input frequency, with an active-high enable input. It is tested in simulation with a test bench and cocotb, and on hardware by enabling the input and observing the output clock with an oscilloscope. No external hardware is needed. The design is a simple clock division experiment with clear documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_KoushikCSN_RISCV.summary: This project implements a simple RISC-V processor that fetches 16-bit instructions, decodes them, performs ALU operations, and writes back to a register file. The design is a basic core that supports a subset of instructions and can be expanded with memory operations and additional control logic. It is intended to be tested with cocotb by applying various instruction sequences and checking the results. The documentation notes that it is not a complete processor and lacks memory operations.
ttihp25a/tt_um_KoushikCSN_RISCV.review_notes: Removed education because the source does not describe an educational purpose.

ttihp25a/tt_um_LFSR_Encrypt.summary: This design implements a simple stream cipher that XORs an 8-bit data input with the output of a linear-feedback shift register. The LFSR value is also provided on the bidirectional pins so that the encrypted output can be decrypted externally by XORing with the same value. The design was verified in simulation by manually calculating LFSR states and checking the encrypted output against expected values. No external hardware is required, and the project is a straightforward demonstration of LFSR-based encryption.

ttihp25a/tt_um_LabA_Group11.summary: This project is a 4-bit by 4-bit array multiplier that takes an 8-bit input, splits it into two 4-bit operands, and produces an 8-bit product. It is built structurally from AND gates and full adders, following the classic array multiplier architecture. The design can be tested by applying an 8-bit input and verifying that the output equals the product of the first and last 4-bit halves of the input. No external hardware is needed, and the documentation includes a diagram of the multiplier.
ttihp25a/tt_um_LabA_Group11.review_notes: Removed alu tag because the source describes only a multiplier, not a general ALU.

ttihp25a/tt_um_MAC_Accelerator_OnSachinS.summary: This project implements a multiplication and accumulation (MAC) operation in Verilog. The documentation states only that it multiplies and accumulates the data. Testing is suggested using a memory operation, and no external hardware is specified. The exact interface and behavior of the design are not fully described in the source.
ttihp25a/tt_um_MAC_Accelerator_OnSachinS.review_notes: Removed unsupported alu and memory tags; kept mac-unit and multiplier, added verilog and insufficient-doc.

ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_canon.summary: This design plays Pachelbel's Canon while displaying synchronized visuals on a VGA screen. It uses a PWM output for audio and requires a Tiny VGA Pmod and a Tiny Audio Pmod. Silicon testing showed it works, though one tester noted the audio was out of sync until manually reset. The design is a demonstration of audio and video capabilities on Tiny Tapeout.
ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_canon.review_notes: Removed generic graphics tag; added silicon-tested and verilog tags supported by the silicon reports and language.

ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_hd_8b10b.summary: This design decodes two 8b10b-encoded serial streams and can optionally multiply the decoded bytes. It uses the K.28.5 comma symbol to establish synchronization and indicates valid data on an output pin. The decoded or multiplied results are presented on the outputs, and the bidirectional pins can be configured as differential pairs when in reset. The design requires no external hardware and is intended for testing high-speed cell libraries.
ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_hd_8b10b.review_notes: Removed encoder because the source describes only decoding, not encoding.

ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_mandelbrot.summary: This design computes and displays the Mandelbrot fractal on a VGA screen using a racing-the-beam technique. It uses 16-bit fixed-point arithmetic and a maximum iteration depth of 14, with configurable position and zoom via input pins. The design requires a Tiny VGA Pmod and a 100 MHz clock. Silicon testing showed it broadly works, though the demo mode can sometimes get stuck zooming into the wrong offset.

ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_rle_vga.summary: This design reads run-length encoded video data from a QSPI flash memory and displays it on a 640x480 VGA output, with PWM audio output. It is intended for playing the Bad Apple music video and requires a QSPI Pmod plugged into an audio Pmod, plus a Tiny VGA Pmod. The design runs at 24 MHz and includes inputs to adjust SPI latency and select the QSPI pinout. Notable limitations include the need for a specific flash command and the requirement to generate the RLE binary file externally.
ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_rle_vga.review_notes: Removed unsupported demoscene tag and added pmod interface tag based on documented external hardware.

ttihp25a/tt_um_MichaelBell_tinyQV.summary: TinyQV is a small RISC-V SoC implementing the RV32EC instruction set with Zcb and Zicond extensions, using QSPI flash for program storage and QSPI PSRAM for data memory. It includes a UART and SPI controller, and is intended to be used with a QSPI PMOD containing flash and RAM, as well as an ST7789 LCD display and game controller. The QSPI clock and data lines are shared between the flash and the RAM, so only one can be accessed simultaneously. Data can be read from flash and RAM, and written to RAM.

ttihp25a/tt_um_NicklausThompson_SkyKing.summary: This project presents an RGB222 VGA signal to the output port. It types some text over an image of a plane flying into the sunset. The design runs automatically and requires a VGA PMOD on the output port. The documentation is very thin and does not provide further implementation details.
ttihp25a/tt_um_NicklausThompson_SkyKing.review_notes: The proposed tags and summary are unrelated to the source documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Nishanth_RISCV.summary: This project implements a simple RISC-V processor that fetches 16-bit instructions, decodes them, performs ALU operations, and writes back to a register file. The design is a basic core that supports a subset of instructions and can be expanded with memory operations and additional control logic. It is intended to be tested with cocotb by applying various instruction sequences and checking the results. The documentation notes that it is not a complete processor and lacks memory operations.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Nishanth_RISCV.review_notes: Removed education because the source does not describe an educational purpose.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Qwendu_spi_fpu.summary: This project is a 32-bit floating point unit accessible over SPI. It features four internal floating point registers that can be written and read over SPI. Every SPI transaction starts with a command byte followed by arguments, and data output requires sending enough bytes to receive the entire response. Testing is best done with the provided Arduino testbench, though the author notes issues with Arduino SPI controllers.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Qwendu_spi_fpu.review_notes: Corrected tags and summary to match the SPI floating point unit described in the source.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Rapoport.summary: This design simulates a single perceptron that takes three inputs, multiplies them by weights, sums the products, and compares the sum to a threshold to produce a binary output. It also accepts a desired output and performs a weight update when the actual output differs, implementing a simple learning rule. The design can be tested by verifying clock and reset operation, but the documentation does not provide detailed test procedures or expected behavior. No external hardware is required.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Richard28277.summary: This project implements a 4-bit ALU that performs arithmetic and logical operations on two 4-bit inputs selected by a 4-bit opcode. It outputs an 8-bit result along with carry-out and overflow status. The design is written in Verilog and can be tested by cycling through opcode values and observing the outputs. The documentation includes a test procedure using the input and output pins.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Richard28277.review_notes: Tags described a spiking neural network; corrected to ALU/arithmetic tags.

ttihp25a/tt_um_SarpHS_array_mult.summary: This project implements a 4-bit multiplier that takes two 4-bit integers and produces an 8-bit product. It uses a manual structural design with AND gates to form partial products and 1-bit full adders to sum them and handle carries. The result is output on an 8-bit output bus. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware.
ttihp25a/tt_um_SarpHS_array_mult.review_notes: Corrected tags and summary to describe the multiplier rather than an ALU.

ttihp25a/tt_um_Strider93.summary: This project implements a digital LIF neuron with reset by subtraction, configurable leakage and threshold. It takes weight inputs and a spike input, and produces a spike output. The documentation is very thin, with no detailed testing instructions beyond inputting weights and spikes to observe spiking.
ttihp25a/tt_um_Strider93.review_notes: Removed floating-point, spi, and adder tags as unsupported; added neuromorphic and spiking-neural-network tags based on the LIF neuron description.

ttihp25a/tt_um_UartMain.summary: This project implements a simple XOR cipher with a UART interface. It receives a character via UART and returns an encrypted character using a configurable key. The key can be updated by asserting the updateKey input before sending the new key. The default key is b10101010.
ttihp25a/tt_um_UartMain.review_notes: Replaced incorrect VGA/video/display/graphics tags with UART, crypto, cipher, and Verilog.

ttihp25a/tt_um_VanceWiberg_top.summary: This design is an 8-bit digital-to-analog converter that uses successive approximation to convert a digital input into an analog output. It requires an external analog comparator and a resistor array to function, as indicated by the pin names and description. The conversion process uses nonlinear sampling, and the design can be tested by providing comparator values and checking the digital outputs. The documentation is brief and does not provide detailed schematics or test results.
ttihp25a/tt_um_VanceWiberg_top.review_notes: Removed sar-adc, analog, and mixed-signal tags not supported by source.

ttihp25a/tt_um_a1k0n_demo.summary: This is a standalone VGA and sound demo that fits in two tiles, developed for the Tiny Tapeout demo competition. It generates a 640x480@60Hz VGA signal with a non-standard 1220-pixel horizontal resolution and RGB222 dithered graphics, plus 3-channel synthesized audio via a 16-bit sigma-delta DAC on a single pin. It requires a 48 MHz clock, a Tiny VGA Pmod for video, and a Tiny Tapeout Audio Pmod or simple RC filter for sound. Silicon tests confirm both graphics and sound work as expected, matching FPGA simulations.

ttihp25a/tt_um_a1k0n_nyancat.summary: This design displays the classic Nyan Cat animation on a VGA monitor with accompanying music. It uses a 2x2 Bayer dithering matrix for color rendition and generates sound from a MIDI file using square waves with exponential decay envelopes, a low-pass filter, and a sigma-delta DAC. It requires a 25.175 MHz clock, a Tiny VGA Pmod for video, and a Tiny Tapeout Audio Pmod or simple RC filter for audio. Silicon tests confirm it works, and it was originally intended for one tile but expanded to two.

ttihp25a/tt_um_a1k0n_vgadonut.summary: This project renders a 3D torus (donut) on a VGA display using a raymarching technique with a CORDIC unit to calculate distances. It runs at a non-standard 1220x480 resolution and uses spatial and temporal dithering to improve appearance despite low horizontal resolution. It requires a 48 MHz clock and a Tiny VGA Pmod for video output. Silicon tests show it works but may have minor glitches at 48 MHz; running at 45 MHz avoids them.
ttihp25a/tt_um_a1k0n_vgadonut.review_notes: Added silicon-tested: the source reports working silicon results from testers and the author.

ttihp25a/tt_um_a3_array_multiplier.summary: This project implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier in Verilog. It generates partial products and sums them column-wise using full adders to produce an 8-bit product. The design is purely combinational and requires no external hardware. It is verified with a Cocotb testbench.
ttihp25a/tt_um_a3_array_multiplier.review_notes: Removed unsupported ALU tag; added combinational and cocotb tags and corrected summary to describe the multiplier.

ttihp25a/tt_um_a_0_array_multiplier.summary: This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit inputs m and q to produce an 8-bit product p. It was created using manual structural design with AND gates and full adders. The full adder module takes three 1-bit inputs and produces a 1-bit sum and carry out. The design generates four 4-bit partial products and sums them to produce the final output.
ttihp25a/tt_um_a_0_array_multiplier.review_notes: The proposed tags and summary are unrelated to the source documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_a_4_array_multiplier.summary: This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier written in Verilog that takes two 4-bit operands and produces an 8-bit product. It generates partial products with AND gates and sums them with full and half adders, following the classic array multiplier structure. The documentation describes simulation-based testing by applying input combinations and comparing the output to expected binary multiplication results. No external hardware is required, and the design is a straightforward educational arithmetic block.
ttihp25a/tt_um_a_4_array_multiplier.review_notes: Removed alu (only multiplication is implemented) and added adder, which the source explicitly mentions.

ttihp25a/tt_um_adder_accumulator_sathwor.summary: This design implements an 8-bit ripple adder and an accumulator register, intended as components for a basic 8-bit CPU. The adder supports two's complement addition and subtraction, and provides zero and carry flags. The accumulator stores the adder output and can drive the bus via tri-state buffers. The design is part of a larger project and requires no external hardware beyond the Tiny Tapeout pins.
ttihp25a/tt_um_adder_accumulator_sathwor.review_notes: Removed alu, register-file, and cpu because the source describes only an adder and accumulator as components of a larger CPU.

ttihp25a/tt_um_aditya_patra.summary: This Verilog design is a priority-encoded state machine with three enable inputs and three corresponding state outputs. Each input must remain asserted for 100000 clock cycles before its state is activated for 100000000 cycles, with priority given to state 1 over 2 over 3. It is intended as the core of a proximity warning system, where LIDAR sensors drive the inputs and buzzers are driven by the outputs. No external hardware is needed for basic testing, but the intended application requires three sensors and three buzzers.
ttihp25a/tt_um_aditya_patra.review_notes: Removed arbiter and industrial; added buzzer and kept sensor-interface for the documented LIDAR/buzzer application.

ttihp25a/tt_um_alf19185_ALU.summary: This project is a 4-bit ALU that performs arithmetic (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and logical operations (AND, OR, NOT, XOR) on two 4-bit inputs. The operation is selected by a 3-bit opcode, and the ALU outputs an 8-bit result along with zero and carry flags. Testing is done by applying the appropriate opcode and inputs. The design requires no external hardware.
ttihp25a/tt_um_alf19185_ALU.review_notes: Removed logic-gate, instruction-decoder, and education because the source describes an opcode-selected ALU without those specific claims.

ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_tt09_ring_osc.summary: This project is a simple ring oscillator implemented by instantiating a sky130 inv_2 inverter ring in Verilog. It provides a single output pin for the oscillator signal. The documentation is minimal, consisting only of the title and one-line description, with no testing details or external hardware requirements. It is likely an experiment to characterize oscillator behavior in the sky130 process.
ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_tt09_ring_osc.review_notes: Removed analog tag because implementation uses digital inverter cells; added process-experiment for characterization intent.

ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_tt09_ring_osc2.summary: This Verilog project implements multiple ring oscillators of different lengths plus simple PWM experiments on a Tiny Tapeout tile. The raw oscillator outputs and divided-down versions are exposed on uo_out, while PWM outputs with selectable duty cycles appear on uio pins when driven by specific ui_in patterns. Testing is done by probing outputs with an oscilloscope and setting ui_in to select PWM duty cycles. The documentation notes that the fastest oscillators may be too fast to measure reliably and that PWM outputs may be noisy due to pad and mux characteristics.
ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_tt09_ring_osc2.review_notes: Removed analog (digital PWM/ring oscillator design) and added clock-divider, which is explicitly documented.

ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_tt09_ring_osc3.summary: This is a resubmission of a ring oscillator design with externally selectable length, controlled by a 3-bit tap input. The raw oscillator output and a divide-by-128 counter output are brought out to pins, allowing frequency measurement with an oscilloscope. The tap input selects between ring lengths of 11 to 1001 inverters, with the shortest ring potentially producing frequencies too high for reliable measurement. The documentation warns that changing the tap while active may cause glitches and suggests setting the tap before activating the design.
ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_tt09_ring_osc3.review_notes: Removed analog; the design is purely digital ring oscillator and counter logic.

ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_vga.summary: This Verilog design generates VGA timing and RGB222 color output for a Tiny VGA PMOD, displaying a bouncing ball animation over an adaptation of Matt Venn's VGA clock. It supports a 640x480 60Hz mode from a 25MHz clock and includes inputs to adjust hours, minutes, and seconds. Testing requires a VGA monitor and Tiny VGA PMOD, with mode and pmod_select inputs configuring the display. The design is notable for combining a real-time clock display with a simple animation and is intended for the IHP tapeout.
ttihp25a/tt_um_algofoogle_vga.review_notes: clock-generator was a misreading of the VGA clock display; added retro for the recreated clock.

ttihp25a/tt_um_alif.summary: This project implements three adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire (ALIF) neurons in Verilog. It receives an 8-bit input current, processes it through the LIF model with adaptive threshold, and outputs spike signals for each neuron along with the internal state of neuron 1. The design requires no external hardware and can be tested by applying input currents and monitoring spike outputs and state variables. The documentation describes the neuron model and testing approach, but the one-line description is marked TODO.
ttihp25a/tt_um_alif.review_notes: Removed neural-network because the design is specifically a spiking neural network, not a generic neural network.

ttihp25a/tt_um_alphaonesoc.summary: AlphaOneSoC is a 32-bit RISC-V SoC based on Michael Bell's TinyQV, implementing the RV32EC ISA. It boots from external QSPI flash or PSRAM and provides UART, SPI, and GPIO interfaces for interaction and debugging. Testing involves flashing instructions into memory and observing outputs via UART, SPI, or GPIO. The design requires a QSPI flash/PSRAM PMOD and is a larger 3x2 tile submission.
ttihp25a/tt_um_alphaonesoc.review_notes: Removed microcontroller (SoC/cpu already cover it) and added multi-tile and qspi, both supported by the pin facts.

ttihp25a/tt_um_anas_7193.summary: This design is a programmable PWM generator implemented in Chisel. It produces a PWM signal whose frequency and duty cycle are set by two 8-bit values, pwm_top and pwm_threshold, encoded on the uio and ui pins respectively. The output frequency is fin/(pwm_top+1) and the duty cycle is (pwm_threshold+1)/(pwm_top+1). Testing requires setting the input pins to desired values and observing the PWM output on an oscilloscope; external switches may be used to set the inputs.

ttihp25a/tt_um_anislam.summary: This design simulates a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) spiking neuron in Verilog. It takes an 8-bit input current and produces an 8-bit state variable and a spike output. The documentation is minimal, with no details on the neuron's parameters or how to test it, and no external hardware is required. The design implements a spiking neural network component on a Tiny Tapeout tile.
ttihp25a/tt_um_anislam.review_notes: Removed generic neural-network tag and added incomplete due to very thin documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_arandomdev_fir_engine_top.summary: FIREngine is a digital FIR filter designed to process audio from an I2S2 PMOD ADC and DAC module. It supports programmable coefficients for low, band, and high pass filtering, with a fixed number of taps determined at synthesis. Coefficients are set via an SDI interface, and the filter uses 2's complement fixed-point arithmetic. Testing requires the I2S2 PMOD and a serial programmer, and the design is intended for audio filtering applications.
ttihp25a/tt_um_arandomdev_fir_engine_top.review_notes: Removed SPI because the source specifies an SDI interface for coefficient programming.

ttihp25a/tt_um_arrayMultFajrSahana.summary: This is a 4x4 bit multiplier designed in Verilog using structural design techniques. It takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product. The design is a lab project (Lab 3) and includes a testbench and Python script for verification. No external hardware is required.
ttihp25a/tt_um_arrayMultFajrSahana.review_notes: Removed education because the source only identifies it as Lab 3 and does not state educational intent.

ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_joe_leighthard.summary: This is a 4-bit array multiplier that takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product. The documentation is very brief, stating only that it splits an 8-bit input into two 4-bit arrays and multiplies them. Testing is described as using various numbers to check multiplicative values, but no detailed methodology or expected results are given. No external hardware is required, and the design appears to be a simple educational arithmetic block.
ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_joe_leighthard.review_notes: Removed alu and structural, which are unsupported by the source.

ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural.summary: This class project implements a 4x4 unsigned array multiplier using carry-save adders followed by a carry-propagate adder. It takes an 8-bit input split into two 4-bit operands and produces an 8-bit product. Testing is done via a Verilog testbench with various input combinations, such as 3*3 and 15*15, comparing outputs to expected results. No external hardware is needed, and the design is a typical educational exercise in structural arithmetic.
ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural.review_notes: Removed alu; the source describes only a multiplier with carry-save and carry-propagate adders.

ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural_Gna.summary: This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit numbers using a series of full adders to produce an 8-bit product. The design is combinational and the documentation includes a block diagram and a testing procedure with example inputs. No external hardware is required.

ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural_sar.summary: This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers to produce an 8-bit product. It uses partial products and full adders to sum them, with carry propagation between stages. The design is verified with a Verilog testbench and Python script, and no external hardware is required.
ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural_sar.review_notes: Removed education tag because the source does not state an educational purpose.

ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural_sec.summary: This project implements a 4-bit array multiplier using structural Verilog. It takes two 4-bit inputs and computes their 8-bit product using partial products and adders. The design is combinational and does not use clock or reset signals. Testing can be done by applying inputs and observing the output, and no external hardware is required.
ttihp25a/tt_um_array_mult_structural_sec.review_notes: Removed education tag because the documentation does not mention teaching or learning intent.

ttihp25a/tt_um_array_secD7.summary: This project implements a 4x4 array multiplier in Verilog that computes the product of two 4-bit binary numbers using partial products and full adders. The multiplier generates partial products by ANDing each bit of one input with all bits of the other, then sums them with full adders in a staged manner. The design is combinational and purely digital, producing an 8-bit product output. It is a structural implementation suitable for learning about binary multiplication.

ttihp25a/tt_um_arry_mult_structural.summary: This project is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit numbers to produce an 8-bit result using partial products and full adders. The documentation describes the structure in detail, including the use of AND gates and full adders to sum partial products. Testing is performed with a testbench that applies various input combinations, including edge cases, and compares outputs to expected binary multiplication results. No external hardware is required, and the design is a standard educational implementation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_arry_mult_structural.review_notes: Removed alu; the source describes only a 4x4 array multiplier.

ttihp25a/tt_um_asgerwenneb.summary: This project is titled 'My Project' and has essentially no documentation, with placeholder text for how it works, how to test, and external hardware. The pin names are generic and provide no information about the design's function. It appears to be an empty or template submission with no described behavior. No meaningful tags or summary can be derived from the available information.

ttihp25a/tt_um_asheldon44_dsm_decimation.summary: This design implements a digital low-pass and decimation filter intended for the output of a delta-sigma analog-to-digital converter. It accepts 1-bit modulator data at 50 MHz and produces 16-bit filtered data on the GPIOs at 781.25 kHz. The analog portion is not included and is hoped for on a future shuttle. It is implemented in Verilog and can be tested by feeding a modulated input and observing the filtered output.
ttihp25a/tt_um_asheldon44_dsm_decimation.review_notes: Removed unsupported FIR/IIR/analog-filter tags; corrected summary to match the documented decimation filter behavior.

ttihp25a/tt_um_atomNPU.summary: AtomNPU is a compact 4-bit neural processing unit that performs multiply-accumulate operations for neural network computations. It takes 4-bit input activations and 4-bit weights and produces a quantized output. The design is intended to be tested with a step-by-step guide, though the provided documentation is minimal. No external hardware is specified, and the design is notable for being a minimal NPU implementation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_atomNPU.review_notes: Removed dsp and fixed-point as unsupported; added edge-ai for the embedded NPU inference target.

ttihp25a/tt_um_b_0_array_multiplier.summary: This project is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that takes two 4-bit binary inputs and produces an 8-bit product. It uses full adders to combine partial products and generate the final multiplication result. The design is implemented in Verilog. It is intended as a lab exercise for a group project.
ttihp25a/tt_um_b_0_array_multiplier.review_notes: Corrected tags and summary to match the array multiplier design.

ttihp25a/tt_um_b_10_array_multiplier.summary: This project implements a 4x4 array multiplier, a combinational digital circuit for multiplying two binary numbers. It generates partial products and adds them using full adders arranged in a systematic array to produce the final product. The design is purely digital and produces an 8-bit product. The source includes a structural description and a diagram of the 4x4 array multiplier.
ttihp25a/tt_um_b_10_array_multiplier.review_notes: Added structural tag because the source describes an array of full adders; corrected the summary wording from 4-bit multiplier to 4x4 array multiplier.

ttihp25a/tt_um_b_12_array_multiplier.summary: This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested via a provided Python testbench where inputs and expected outputs are set. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.
ttihp25a/tt_um_b_12_array_multiplier.review_notes: Removed education tag because the source does not state a teaching or learning purpose.

ttihp25a/tt_um_b_2_array_multiplier.summary: This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested via simulation with a testbench covering five test cases including minimum and maximum values to verify carry propagation. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.
ttihp25a/tt_um_b_2_array_multiplier.review_notes: Removed education tag because the source does not state a teaching or learning purpose.

ttihp25a/tt_um_b_6_array_multiplier.summary: This project implements a 4x4 array multiplier that takes two 4-bit inputs, m and q, and produces an 8-bit product p. Partial products are generated by ANDing each bit of m with all bits of q and summed with a series of full adders. The design is purely combinational and produces an 8-bit product. It is a structural implementation suitable for learning about binary multiplication.
ttihp25a/tt_um_b_6_array_multiplier.review_notes: Added structural tag; summary corrected to match the documented 4x4 inputs and 8-bit output.

ttihp25a/tt_um_b_8_array_multiplier.summary: This is a 4x4 structural array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested by applying input pairs covering typical, edge, and corner cases, and verifying the 8-bit product. The design requires no external hardware and is a straightforward educational project demonstrating binary multiplication.
ttihp25a/tt_um_b_8_array_multiplier.review_notes: Removed education tag because the source does not state a teaching or learning purpose.

ttihp25a/tt_um_benpayne_ps2_decoder.summary: This PS2 decoder reads scan codes from a PS2 keyboard, debounces and synchronizes the signals, and outputs the data byte along with valid, interrupt, and data-ready signals. It includes a FIFO to queue received bytes, and the host can read data by asserting chip select. It requires a PS2 keyboard and level shifting from 5V to 3.3V, and is intended for interfacing with retro computers. The design is a straightforward implementation of the PS2 protocol.
ttihp25a/tt_um_benpayne_ps2_decoder.review_notes: Removed 'decoder' because it is a type tag for code-to-signal decoding, not a PS/2 protocol decoder; no canonical replacement exists.

ttihp25a/tt_um_betz_morse_keyer.summary: The Morse Code Keyer converts a keyed CW input from a straight key or iambic paddle into Morse code tones and a 7-segment character display. It supports iambic modes A and B, adjustable speed from 7 to 110 WPM, and outputs auxiliary dit/dah signals for radio equipment. It requires external paddles and a radio interface, and includes a companion PCB design. The documentation warns against using the auxiliary Morse output directly as a raw radio TX control.
ttihp25a/tt_um_betz_morse_keyer.review_notes: Removed unsupported text tag, added dip-switch and pmod, and replaced the unsupported 'notable' claim with the documented warning.

ttihp25a/tt_um_bilal_trng.summary: This is a true random number generator that samples a noise source with a digital circuit and conditions the data using SHA-256 to produce cryptographic-quality random numbers. It supports raw entropy output for analysis and hashed output for secure applications, with built-in health tests such as the repetition count test. A state machine controls data collection, processing, and transmission of results over UART. Testing requires a UART terminal, and optionally an oscilloscope for debugging the noise source.
ttihp25a/tt_um_bilal_trng.review_notes: Removed bist (health tests are entropy health checks, not chip self-test); no silicon-tested claim since no silicon reports exist.

ttihp25a/tt_um_bitty.summary: This is a 16-bit simple processor with UART receive and transmit data pins and baud-rate selection inputs. The documentation is very thin and does not describe the instruction set, architecture, or internal blocks. UART communication is emulated within the testbench, and no external hardware is required. The design has been resubmitted on multiple shuttle runs but has no silicon test reports.
ttihp25a/tt_um_bitty.review_notes: Corrected tags and summary to match the thin UART processor documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_brailliance.summary: Brailliance converts an ASCII character into its 8-bit Braille representation, where the first two bits of each output byte are zeroed for redundancy. The design is implemented in Verilog and uses a 5 MHz clock. External hardware such as LEDs or solenoid actuators can be used to display the Braille output. This project serves as an educational tool for ASCII-to-Braille conversion.
ttihp25a/tt_um_brailliance.review_notes: Removed display and education tags as they are not supported by the source.

ttihp25a/tt_um_branch_pred.summary: This is a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor that reads branch instruction addresses and ground truth directions via SPI and outputs predictions. It is based on a research paper and uses latch-based memory, with a functional simulation in C++ and CocoTB tests. It requires external hardware to drive inputs and read outputs, and is notable for its use of a perceptron model and detailed debugging features.

ttihp25a/tt_um_brandonramos_VGA_Pong_wit.summary: The design implements a two-player Pong game that uses two NES controllers for input and outputs a VGA video signal.
ttihp25a/tt_um_brandonramos_VGA_Pong_wit.review_notes: Removed gpio tag because the bidirectional pins are dedicated to NES controller signals.

ttihp25a/tt_um_brukstus_tdc_with_spi.summary: This is a time-to-digital converter with an SPI interface, based on a previous ALU design. It includes pins for SPI communication and start/stop signals, and outputs a busy signal. The documentation is very thin, referring to an external GitHub repository for testing details. No external hardware is required, but the design's functionality and testing are not well described.
ttihp25a/tt_um_brukstus_tdc_with_spi.review_notes: Removed unsupported instrumentation tag and added insufficient-doc for the very thin documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_bytex64_munch.summary: Munch displays a munching squares animation on a VGA monitor while generating simple music through an audio PMOD. It uses the Tiny VGA and TT Audio pinouts and is implemented in Verilog. The author notes it works but requires a manual reset to sync the music properly. The design targets a 25.175 MHz input clock and was tested on fabricated silicon with partial success.
ttihp25a/tt_um_bytex64_munch.review_notes: Added silicon-tested, audio, and music; expanded summary to four sentences.

ttihp25a/tt_um_c13_array_mult.summary: This project implements a 4x4 multiplier in structural Verilog, producing an 8-bit product from two 4-bit inputs. It is built from an array of full adders that combine partial products, following a classic textbook multiplier structure. The design is intended as a lab exercise and is tested by applying input pairs and comparing the output to the expected product. No external hardware is required, and the documentation is sufficient to understand the basic operation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_c13_array_mult.review_notes: Removed alu tag; added combinational tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_c1_array_mult_structural.summary: This is a 4x4 array multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to sum partial products. It is tested by applying different input combinations and comparing outputs to expected results. The design requires no external hardware and is an educational project demonstrating binary multiplication. The documentation describes the partial-product generation and carry handling used to produce the 8-bit result.
ttihp25a/tt_um_c1_array_mult_structural.review_notes: Removed structural tag; source describes an educational array multiplier, not a structural HDL style.

ttihp25a/tt_um_c7_array_mult.summary: This project is a 4-bit multiplier that multiplies two 4-bit binary numbers using full adders to produce an 8-bit product. It is tested by specifying two 4-bit inputs in a Python test script and verifying the output against the expected product. The design requires no external hardware. The documentation is brief but sufficient to describe the function and testing method.
ttihp25a/tt_um_c7_array_mult.review_notes: Removed alu tag; added combinational tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_c_2_array_mult.summary: This is a 4x4 array multiplier implemented in Verilog that multiplies two 4-bit numbers to produce an 8-bit product. The design is based on a standard array multiplier structure using full adders. Testing is performed by adding test cases in a Python script and following the instructions in the test README. No external hardware is required, and the documentation is minimal but adequate.
ttihp25a/tt_um_c_2_array_mult.review_notes: Removed alu tag; added combinational tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_c_4_4b_mult.summary: This project implements a 4-bit multiplier that takes two 4-bit inputs and produces an 8-bit product using full adders. The inputs are split into two 4-bit portions, and the multiplication is performed through adder logic. Testing is done using a testbench with idle cases. No external hardware is needed, but the documentation is very sparse and lacks detail on the exact implementation and test procedure.
ttihp25a/tt_um_c_4_4b_mult.review_notes: Removed alu tag (design is a multiplier only) and added incomplete for the very thin documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_carryskip_adder8.summary: This design is an 8-bit carry-skip adder that adds two 8-bit numbers using a combination of ripple-carry and skip logic to reduce carry propagation delay. The adder is divided into two 4-bit sections, and the final sum is registered and output synchronously with the clock. Testing involves applying input values to the ui_in and uio_in pins and verifying the sum on uo_out after each clock edge. No external hardware is required, and the documentation provides a clear explanation of the operation and test method.
ttihp25a/tt_um_carryskip_adder8.review_notes: Removed alu tag; added combinational tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_carryskip_adder9.summary: This project implements an 8-bit carry-skip adder that adds two 8-bit numbers using ripple-carry and skip logic for improved performance. The design splits the addition into two 4-bit sections and registers the output in sync with the clock. Testing is done by applying inputs to ui_in and uio_in and checking the sum on uo_out after each rising edge. No external hardware is needed, and the documentation is identical to another project, suggesting it may be a duplicate or shared design.
ttihp25a/tt_um_carryskip_adder9.review_notes: Removed alu tag; added combinational tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_cattuto_sr_latch.summary: This experiment implements a 512-bit shift register using D latches instead of flip-flops, with a single pulse rippling through the register to perform the shift. It has one input, one output, and an edge-triggered control signal that updates the shift on either a rising or falling edge. Testing involves shifting zeros in until the register is empty, then shifting in a pattern and observing it appear on the output after 512 control transitions. No external hardware is required.
ttihp25a/tt_um_cattuto_sr_latch.review_notes: Added incomplete because the source explicitly frames the design as an experiment.

ttihp25a/tt_um_ccu_goatgate.summary: This project is a tiny encryption core that takes a 4-bit input and a 4-bit key to produce a 4-bit encrypted output. It is intended to be tested by sending randomized 4-bit inputs and keys and observing the output. The design requires no external hardware, though memory may be needed to supply test data. The documentation is very limited, providing only a high-level description without details on the encryption algorithm or test methodology.
ttihp25a/tt_um_ccu_goatgate.review_notes: Removed unsupported security tag and added verilog tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_cdc_test.summary: This design is a VGA demo that displays an image of a plane flying into the sunset. It runs automatically and outputs VGA signals on the uo pins, requiring a VGA PMOD connected to the output. The project is a re-run of a previous demo and mentions an unsuccessful attempt at a clock domain crossing project. The documentation is minimal, focusing on the visual output rather than technical details.
ttihp25a/tt_um_cdc_test.review_notes: Removed unsupported 'text' tag and added 'silicon-tested' based on the TT08 re-run statement.

ttihp25a/tt_um_cejmu.summary: This design bundles four educational modules selected by an internal multiplexer: a vending machine state machine, a coin acceptor decoder, a 24-bit ripple carry adder, and a 24-bit carry lookahead adder. The adders are tested by feeding 24-bit operands in 8-bit chunks and reading the 25-bit result in 8-bit chunks. An oscilloscope can be used to measure the difference in execution speed between the two adder types. The coin acceptor decoder is designed for the HX-916 model.
ttihp25a/tt_um_cejmu.review_notes: Removed multiplexer tag as it is an internal selection mechanism, not a primary design feature.

ttihp25a/tt_um_cellular_alchemist.summary: This project implements a Hopfield neural network on-chip using Izhikevich-type regular spiking and fast spiking neurons with on-chip Hebbian learning for pattern storage and retrieval. It accepts a learning enable signal and a 4-bit pattern input, and outputs spikes from seven neurons via bidirectional pins. The design is a leaky integrate-and-fire neuron model and is intended to be tested, though the documentation provides little detail on the test procedure. No external hardware is required, but the documentation is sparse and lacks specifics on operation and verification.
ttihp25a/tt_um_cellular_alchemist.review_notes: Removed machine-learning tag (neuromorphic spiking design) and added incomplete for the sparse documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_cfib_demo.summary: This demoscene competition entry generates a pseudo-random soundtrack via PWM and displays a waveform on a VGA monitor. It uses the Tiny VGA Pmod on uo_out and Mike's audio Pmod on uio_out[7]. The design is written in Verilog and runs from a 50 MHz clock with asynchronous reset. A silicon test report confirms the design is working.
ttihp25a/tt_um_cfib_demo.review_notes: Removed waveform-generator (not a general waveform generator) and added silicon-tested per the working test report.

ttihp25a/tt_um_chip4lyfe.summary: This design implements a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron network inspired by snnTorch. It accepts an 8-bit input current split between two input neurons, and each neuron integrates the current, decays its state by bit-shifting each clock cycle, and emits a spike when its state reaches or exceeds a threshold of 8. The network has multiple layers, with spike outputs for each layer and state variable outputs for the output layer neurons. The documentation provides no testing procedure or external hardware requirements, and the design is a compact digital implementation of a spiking neural network building block.

ttihp25a/tt_um_chip_rom.summary: This design implements a 256-byte ROM that stores information about the Tiny Tapeout chip, including the shuttle name and commit hash. The first 16 bytes are 7-segment encoded and can be displayed on the on-board 7-segment display by holding reset low and toggling the clock, or by setting the address with DIP switches. The ROM is 8-bit wide and 256 bytes long. It is intended to provide chip information via ROM access and display.
ttihp25a/tt_um_chip_rom.review_notes: Removed unsupported counter and education tags; added rom, memory, 7-segment, and verilog; adjusted summary to remove educational claim.

ttihp25a/tt_um_claudiotalarico_counter.summary: This project is a 4-bit up/down binary counter with enable and test mode. It uses input pins for test, up/down selection, and enable, and outputs the 4-bit count value. Testing requires connecting the enable pin to VDD, test to GND, up/down to a switch, reset to an RC startup circuit, and a 50 MHz clock, with the outputs connected to LEDs. The design is a straightforward digital building block with minimal documentation beyond basic operation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_claudiotalarico_counter.review_notes: Removed dip-switch tag; the source only mentions a generic switch.

ttihp25a/tt_um_clock_divider_arghunter.summary: This design is a clock divider with lag correction that interfaces with PDM microphones and an I2S receiver. It takes bit clock and LR clock inputs, along with PDM data from up to eight microphones, and outputs PCM audio for each microphone plus a beamformed PCM output. The documentation is too vague to describe its exact operation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_clock_divider_arghunter.review_notes: Removed unsupported i2s/dsp tags and added pdm based on PDM microphone inputs.

ttihp25a/tt_um_comm_ic_bhavuk.summary: Comm_IC combines UART, SPI, and I2C communication protocols into a single design that is selected via input data bits.
ttihp25a/tt_um_comm_ic_bhavuk.review_notes: Added missing canonical tags for the implemented communication protocols and language.

ttihp25a/tt_um_control_block.summary: This design implements the control block for an 8-bit CPU based on the SAP-1 architecture. It uses a 6-stage sequential counter and a lookup table to generate control signals from a 4-bit opcode, with outputs for various register and memory control lines as well as a halt signal. Testing involves applying opcodes and monitoring the control signal outputs, optionally using a logic analyzer or slowing the clock. The project is part of a course (ECE 298A) and is intended to be integrated with other CPU sub-blocks.
ttihp25a/tt_um_control_block.review_notes: Removed instruction-decoder as the block is a control unit; added sequential-logic for the micro-instruction counter.

ttihp25a/tt_um_couchand_cora16.summary: CORA-16 is a 16-bit CPU that uses external SPI memory for instruction fetch and execution. It features a byte-wide general-purpose input and output bus, and supports single-stepping for debugging via a step pin. Status pins indicate busy, halt, and trap conditions, with trap recovery possible by stepping. The design requires an external SPI RAM, such as a Raspberry Pi acting as an emulator, to load and run programs.
ttihp25a/tt_um_couchand_cora16.review_notes: Removed memory tag because the design uses external SPI RAM rather than implementing memory; added instruction-decoder as core CPU logic.

ttihp25a/tt_um_crispy_vga.summary: Crispy VGA takes a standard Tiny Tapeout VGA signal as input and adds a programmable amount of random noise to the video and audio signals before passing them to the output. The uio_in[0] through uio_in[4] inputs individually toggle noise on the hsync, B, G, R, and vsync signals. The uio_in[5] input sets the noise level applied to the R, G, and B wires to high or low, and the uio_in[0:5] inputs set successively increasing noise levels on the audio signal. Testing requires plugging an existing Tiny Tapeout VGA project into the input, connecting the output to a VGA monitor, and selecting the control bits for the desired noise level.
ttihp25a/tt_um_crispy_vga.review_notes: Summary expanded to four sentences covering the documented noise controls and test setup.

ttihp25a/tt_um_d_4_array_multiplier.summary: This design implements a 4x4 structural array multiplier in Verilog that multiplies two 4-bit numbers to produce an 8-bit product. It generates partial products using two-input AND gates and sums them column by column with full adders, propagating carries between stages. The design is purely combinational and is intended as an educational exercise for a university digital design course. Testing is done by applying 8-bit input values and comparing the output to the expected product.
ttihp25a/tt_um_d_4_array_multiplier.review_notes: Removed unsupported ML/DSP/MAC tags and replaced the invented DLFloat MAC summary with the actual 4x4 array multiplier description.

ttihp25a/tt_um_daobaanh_rng.summary: This design is a trial implementation of a lightweight all-digital true random number generator based on ring oscillators. It outputs random data via a UART serial interface, and also provides ring oscillator and random generator outputs for observation. The design is intended for testing and evaluation of TRNG concepts. It uses ring oscillators to generate entropy.
ttihp25a/tt_um_daobaanh_rng.review_notes: Removed prng and crypto tags; added ring-oscillator and uart, which are directly supported by the pins and description.

ttihp25a/tt_um_daosvik_aesinvsbox.summary: This circuit computes the inverse S-box of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). It takes an 8-bit input byte on ui[0] through ui[7] and produces an 8-bit output byte on uo[0] through uo[7]. The result can be read back from uo_out (unregistered) or uio_out (registered). No external hardware is required.
ttihp25a/tt_um_daosvik_aesinvsbox.review_notes: Removed lookup-table tag as unsupported; summary expanded to four supported sentences.

ttihp25a/tt_um_db_MAC.summary: This design implements an 8-bit multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit for unsigned integers using Vedic multipliers and reversible gates. Inputs are registered on half a clock cycle, and the MAC operation is performed with the multiplier and adder each taking half a clock cycle. The result is output on dedicated and bidirectional pins. The project explores reversible gates for energy efficiency and requires no external hardware.
ttihp25a/tt_um_db_MAC.review_notes: Removed low-power because the source only mentions exploring reversible gates for energy efficiency, not a low-power implementation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_ddc_arghunter.summary: This design converts I2S audio input to PDM output using an inverted CIC filter and modulator. It also supports up to eight PDM microphones, producing per-microphone PCM outputs and a beamformed PCM output, with delay selection controlled by five pins. The design is intended for use with an I2S output device and PDM input devices, such as microphones and a clock generator. The documentation is minimal beyond the pin descriptions and a brief explanation of the core conversion method.
ttihp25a/tt_um_ddc_arghunter.review_notes: Removed unsupported fir-filter and delay-line tags; added sigma-delta for the PDM modulator.

ttihp25a/tt_um_delta_liafn.summary: This design implements a delta recurrent neural network (Delta RNN) combined with a leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron. It accepts an 8-bit input current, computes the difference between previous and current states, and generates a spike when that difference exceeds a set delta threshold. Outputs include the state variable and the difference in states. The documentation provides no testing procedure or external hardware requirements, and the design is a compact digital implementation of a spiking neural network component.

ttihp25a/tt_um_demosiine_sda.summary: DemoSiine is a demoscene-style audio-visual project that generates a 640x480 VGA video signal and a looping ~28 second audio track. The video output includes dynamic wavy sine layers and a rainbowy overlay, with user controls to enable/disable layers, pause the animation, and toggle styles. The audio engine drives a frequency synthesizer to produce the soundtrack. It requires external hardware: a TinyVGA PMOD for video output, a TT Audio PMOD for audio output, and switches for input control.
ttihp25a/tt_um_demosiine_sda.review_notes: Removed button (inputs are switches); added pmod, music, and video to match the PMOD hardware and audio/video outputs.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dendraws_donut.summary: The donut project displays a rendered donut on a VGA screen. It uses hand-crafted ellipses to create the donut shape and outputs a standard VGA signal with 2-bit RGB color, horizontal sync, and vertical sync. The design operates with a 50.35 MHz clock and requires a TinyVGA PMOD connected to the output pins for display. The documentation is sparse, providing only a brief description and testing instructions.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dendraws_donut.review_notes: Removed demoscene as unsupported; added pmod because the TinyVGA PMOD is required.

ttihp25a/tt_um_devinatkin_basys3_uart.summary: This design runs the main Basys 3 peripherals over a 115200 UART link. It handles 16 LED inputs, 16 switch outputs, 12 seven-segment display inputs, and 5 button outputs, communicating via UART RX and TX on the bidirectional PMOD bus. The UART messages use prefixes such as LD, SW, 7S, and BT to identify the peripheral data. It is implemented in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout platform.
ttihp25a/tt_um_devinatkin_basys3_uart.review_notes: Removed direct peripheral tags since all peripherals are accessed over UART; added uart, pmod, and fpga tags.

ttihp25a/tt_um_devmonk_ay8913.summary: This Verilog implementation is a replica of the classic AY-3-8913 programmable sound generator, a 3-voice PSG chip from General Instrument. It provides three square-wave tone generators, a white noise generator using a 17-bit LFSR, an envelope generator with 10 shapes, and 16 volume levels, controlled through 14 registers. The design outputs digital 8-bit audio and a PWM pseudo-analog audio signal, and can be configured with an external clock divider. It is intended for hardware preservation and educational purposes, with a test suite for regression testing against the original chip behavior.
ttihp25a/tt_um_devmonk_ay8913.review_notes: Replaced incorrect neural-network/machine-learning/decoder tags with sound-generator, music, audio, pwm, lfsr, verilog, retro, and dac based on the source.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dff_mem.summary: This project implements a 16-byte RAM built from D flip-flops. It supports read and write operations with a 4-bit address, active-low chip enable and load signals, and an 8-bit data input. Read operations are asynchronous, and the output is high-impedance when not enabled. The design is intended for integration into an 8-bit processor and includes CocoTB testbenches that verify write and read functionality across all addresses.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dff_mem.review_notes: Removed sram (built from DFFs) and added cocotb per documented testbenches.

ttihp25a/tt_um_digital_clock_example.summary: This design implements a digital desk clock that displays hours, minutes, and seconds in 24-hour format. It uses SPI to drive a MAX7219 7-segment display driver because there are not enough output pins to directly control six 7-segment displays. The time can be set using dedicated buttons for hours and minutes, with a fast/slow adjustment mode and a 12-hour mode option. The design requires an external MAX7219 module and a 32.768 kHz reference clock for accurate timekeeping.
ttihp25a/tt_um_digital_clock_example.review_notes: Removed rtc and clock-generator tags that are not supported by the source.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dlfloatmac.summary: This design implements a MAC unit for the 16-bit DL float data type. Inputs are fed as binary or hexadecimal representations of the floating-point format, and outputs are read similarly. An FPGA is required to drive the inputs and capture the 16-bit result, which arrives as 8 bits over two clock cycles. It is implemented in Verilog and spans two tiles.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dlfloatmac.review_notes: Replaced incorrect audio tags with MAC/floating-point/DSP tags and corrected summary to match the DL float MAC description.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dlmiles_dffram32x8_2r1w.summary: This project implements a 32x8 dual-port-read single-port-write RAM using D-type flip-flops, described by the author as a 'really bad implementation' due to its inefficiency. The RAM has two read ports (A and B) and one write port (A), with configurable features such as read buffering, write-through policy, and page selection via configuration bits latched on reset release. It is intended to be tested with standard Tiny Tapeout hardware and an RP2040, and a MicroPython interface is planned. The design is notable for its use of flip-flops instead of dedicated RAM blocks and its flexible read/write policies.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dlmiles_dffram32x8_2r1w.review_notes: Removed register-file (it is a RAM array, not a register file) and added sram as the canonical memory-block tag.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dlmiles_poc_fskmodem_hdlc.summary: This project is a proof-of-concept digital FSK modem with HDLC framing and UART interface, targeting amateur radio packet communication at data rates from 4800 to 64000 baud. It uses a lookup-table-based waveform generator for 2FSK modulation and includes UART flow control signals. The design is intended to be paired with a future CPU to form a complete terminal node controller (TNC). Testing requires external hardware such as an RP2040 or FPGA to validate the interface.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dlmiles_poc_fskmodem_hdlc.review_notes: Removed rom (only in original hardware description) and added demodulator and incomplete.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dlmiles_tt08_poc_uart.summary: The UART project is a UART data terminal equipment (DTE) implementation in SpinalHDL. It provides standard UART signals such as TxD, RxD, RTS, CTS, DSR, DCD, DTR, and RI, along with interrupt outputs. The design is intended to connect to a standard Tiny Tapeout PCB and interface with an RP2040's UART. Documentation is minimal, with only pin mappings and a brief note that docs are to follow.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dmtd_arghunter.summary: This design is a Dual Mixer Time Differential (DMTD) system with multiple PDM microphone inputs and PCM outputs. It includes delay select inputs and a beamformed PCM output, suggesting microphone array beamforming. The documentation is sparse, but the pin names indicate a digital signal processing application for audio capture. It is implemented in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout platform.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dmtd_arghunter.review_notes: The proposed tags were unsupported by the source; corrected to reflect the documented DMTD/microphone beamforming design.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dog_BILBO.summary: This design implements an 8-bit Concurrent Built-In Logic Block Observer (CBILBO) for memory testing, using shift registers, multiplexers, and feedback logic. It provides a way to observe and control internal memory elements for test purposes. The project includes input and output paths for Tiny Tapeout and supports asynchronous reset. No external hardware is required for testing, and the design is intended to be verified through simulation of its shifting and feedback behavior.
ttihp25a/tt_um_dog_BILBO.review_notes: Removed scan-chain (unsupported); added bist, shift-register, and memory.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dpmu.summary: This project is titled DPMU (Dynamic Power Management Unit) and is implemented in SystemVerilog. The pin names are generic, and there is no documentation describing its functionality, interface, or how it should be tested. The clock is specified as 100 Hz, which is unusually low and may indicate an error or a very slow control loop. Due to the lack of documentation, it is not possible to provide a meaningful summary.

ttihp25a/tt_um_dpmunit.summary: This project is titled DPM_Unit and is described as a Design and Implementation of Dynamic Power management unit, implemented in SystemVerilog. The pin names are generic, and there is no documentation describing its functionality, interface, or how it should be tested. The clock is specified as 100 Hz, which is unusually low and may indicate an error or a very slow control loop. Due to the lack of documentation, it is not possible to provide a meaningful summary.

ttihp25a/tt_um_drum_goekce.summary: This design consists of a RAM and an approximate multiplier based on the DRUM technique for approximate applications. It multiplies two operands a and b to produce a result r, with operands and results accessed through an address-mapped RAM. The design is written in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout platform. The documentation notes that product results may differ if the frequency is increased, suggesting approximate behavior under timing variation.
ttihp25a/tt_um_drum_goekce.review_notes: Corrected completely unrelated VGA/video tags and summary to match actual DRUM approximate multiplier with RAM.

ttihp25a/tt_um_ece298a_8_bit_cpu_top.summary: This is an 8-bit CPU based on the SAP-1 architecture, developed as part of a university course. It includes a control unit, program counter, instruction register, 16-byte memory, arithmetic logic unit with carry and zero flags, accumulator, and output register. The CPU can execute a small instruction set and provides outputs for the accumulator and flags. It is intended for educational purposes and can be tested by providing opcodes and observing outputs.
ttihp25a/tt_um_ece298a_8_bit_cpu_top.review_notes: Removed unsupported register-file tag; added risc-v tag noting the architecture is not RISC-V, correcting a potential misattribution.

ttihp25a/tt_um_edwintorok.summary: This project is a demoscene competition entry that implements a limited-precision ray tracer in two Tiny Tapeout tiles, embracing rounding errors as its primary feature. The RTL was written in HardCaml, which emits Verilog that is committed to the source tree. It renders 640x480 at 60 Hz with the eye Z coordinate animated between 3.5 and 4.5 over 256 frames, and outputs VGA on uo[0-7] plus a simple hsync/vsync audio mix on uio[7]. Setting ui[0] to 0 runs the default demo and setting it to 1 shows a color-bar test image, with an external 25.25 MHz clock required.
ttihp25a/tt_um_edwintorok.review_notes: Proposed tags and summary described an unrelated counter/7-segment design; replaced with the documented HardCaml ray tracer demoscene entry.

ttihp25a/tt_um_emilian_muxpga.summary: This project is a resubmission of a TinyFPGA design for Tiny Tapeout 8, implemented in Verilog. It provides four inputs, two command pins, and eight outputs, and is configured and then observed via the outputs. No special external hardware is required, and the design includes tests. The documentation is very brief, so the exact function of the FPGA configuration is not detailed.
ttihp25a/tt_um_emilian_muxpga.review_notes: Removed unsupported education and template tags; added incomplete due to very thin documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_emmyxu_obstacle_detection.summary: This Verilog design takes two sensor inputs and a reset, and outputs two signals intended for motors or buzzers. It compares each sensor value against a threshold and, if only one side is active, sends a signal to the opposite motor; if both are active, it sends a signal to both motors. Testing involves driving the sensor pins with 0 or 1 and reading the outputs; a reset pin clears all outputs. External hardware includes ultrasonic sensors, a microcontroller, and haptic motors.

ttihp25a/tt_um_enjens.summary: This Verilog design is a clock-driven counter intended to display values on a 7-segment display. The documentation is very thin and does not describe the exact counting or display logic. It uses a 1 Hz clock and has eight outputs that likely drive the display segments. No silicon test results are reported.
ttihp25a/tt_um_enjens.review_notes: Removed unsupported factory-test and current-mirror tags; added 7-segment, clock-divider, and insufficient-doc.

ttihp25a/tt_um_ephrenm_tsal.summary: This design implements the Tractive System Active Light (TSAL) function for a Formula SAE electric vehicle, as required by FSAE rule EV.5.9. It reads a 12-bit value from an external AD7476A ADC via a serial interface and compares it to a threshold; if below the threshold, it drives a green LED continuously, and if above, it flashes a red LED at 4 Hz. Testing requires a PMOD AD1 and simulation for at least one second to verify blink timing. The design is intended to be hard-wired in the vehicle and uses a Tiny Tapeout chip for the digital logic.
ttihp25a/tt_um_ephrenm_tsal.review_notes: Removed timer tag; the blink function is part of the TSAL logic, not a separate timer peripheral.

ttihp25a/tt_um_ezchips_calc.summary: This is an 8-bit calculator design originating from a ChipCraft lab exercise. It is implemented in Verilog and tested using Makerchip simulation. No external hardware is required, and all pins are marked unused in the provided pin list. The documentation is minimal, consisting only of a one-line description and a note about simulation testing.
ttihp25a/tt_um_ezchips_calc.review_notes: Removed unsupported alu and education tags; added incomplete due to minimal documentation and unused pins.

ttihp25a/tt_um_factory_test.summary: This design has been validated on fabricated silicon and works as expected. It is a factory test module that can test all the I/O pins of the ASIC. It has three modes: mirroring input pins to outputs, mirroring bidirectional pins to outputs, and outputting an 8-bit counter on both output and bidirectional pins. It is implemented in Verilog and targets the Tiny Tapeout platform.
ttihp25a/tt_um_factory_test.review_notes: Removed unsupported education tag and added factory-test, counter, and gpio tags.

ttihp25a/tt_um_faramire_rotary_ring_wrap.summary: This Verilog design uses a rotary encoder to control a ring of 12 WS2812B LEDs. Rotating the encoder selects which LED is lit, and a button inverts the LED state. The user can select the color (green, red, or blue) via three input pins and set the intensity with two additional pins. The chip outputs a WS2812B serial data stream on one pin to drive the LED chain, and it also outputs the current count value. External hardware includes a rotary encoder and a WS2812B LED ring.

ttihp25a/tt_um_faramire_stopwatch.summary: This is a simple stopwatch that counts in hundredths of a second and displays the time on an 8-digit 7-segment display via SPI using a MAX7219 chip. It includes start/stop, lap time, and reset inputs, with outputs for SPI MOSI, CS, and CLK, as well as status signals. The design divides a 1 MHz clock to 100 Hz to drive the counters. External hardware needed includes buttons for control and a MAX7219-compatible display.

ttihp25a/tt_um_favoritohjs_scroller.summary: This design generates a scrolling pixelated cityscape video signal for VGA output. The terrain layers are produced using an LFSR to create deterministic randomness. It requires a Tiny VGA carrier board and a 25.18 MHz clock to display video. Silicon testing confirmed it works and produces a Tetris-like scrolling display.
ttihp25a/tt_um_favoritohjs_scroller.review_notes: Removed demoscene tag; the source does not describe a demoscene-style showcase.

ttihp25a/tt_um_find_the_damn_issue.summary: This 2x2 tile design is a USB to UART/SPI/I2C/JTAG/GPIO adapter implemented in Gatery. It enumerates as a USB CDC device on a host computer and can bit-bang various serial protocols to communicate with external devices. Testing involves connecting a device such as a LIS2DH12 sensor and running example software. An external 1.5k pull-up resistor on USB_DP is required for USB operation. The design is notable for supporting many protocols on a single chip.

ttihp25a/tt_um_flummer_ltc.summary: This design generates Linear Timecode (LTC) for audio and video synchronisation, using counters to track time and frame count and serialising 80-bit biphase mark coded frames. It is driven by a 12 MHz clock and starts counting from 00:00:00:00 after reset, with the frame rate selected by two input pins for 24, 25, or 30 fps. The LTC output appears on a bidirectional pin and can be fed to an audio PMOD for levels usable by audio equipment, or connected directly to a logic analyser. The 29.97 fps mode is documented as not implemented, and the project is a small single-tile Verilog design.
ttihp25a/tt_um_flummer_ltc.review_notes: Removed synchronizer (not a CDC block) and added signal-generator for the LTC waveform output.

ttihp25a/tt_um_flyingfish800.summary: This is a simple Verilog test project that accumulates the value on the dedicated input pins into an internal register every clock cycle. The least significant bits of the accumulated value are output on the dedicated output pins, while the most significant bits are output on the bidirectional pins. It is intended as a basic demonstration and requires switches on inputs and LEDs on outputs for testing. The design is minimal and serves as a template or experiment.
ttihp25a/tt_um_flyingfish800.review_notes: Removed alu, register-file, counter, and education tags because the source describes only a simple accumulator/test design.

ttihp25a/tt_um_fountaincoder_top_ad.summary: This Verilog design implements a temporal adder, where addition is performed over time with an enable signal. It takes 8 input bits and produces 8 output bits, and is intended to be used as a coprocessor for vector calculations driven by an RP2040. The design was tested using cocotb. No external hardware is required beyond the driving microcontroller.
ttihp25a/tt_um_fountaincoder_top_ad.review_notes: Removed accelerator tag because the source describes a coprocessor, not a dedicated compute accelerator.

ttihp25a/tt_um_four_bit_multiplier_nasan.summary: This project is a 4-bit multiplier that takes two 4-bit integers and outputs a single 8-bit integer. It was created using manual structural design with AND gates and 1-bit full adders. The partial products are aligned diagonally to mimic manual binary multiplication. The project was created for NYU's digital logic course Lab 4.
ttihp25a/tt_um_four_bit_multiplier_nasan.review_notes: The proposed tags and summary are unrelated to the source documentation.

ttihp25a/tt_um_frequency_counter.summary: This design measures the frequency of an external signal by counting pulses over 100 ms periods and displays the result on a 128x32 SSD1306 OLED display using an emulated 7-segment format. It requires an external 1 MHz clock, a PMOD OLED display, and the signal to be measured connected to the input pin. The design is implemented in SystemVerilog and uses SPI to communicate with the OLED. No silicon test results are provided, so the actual performance is not documented.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gamepad_pmod_demo.summary: This project reads input from a Gamepad PMOD and displays the pressed buttons as green symbols on a VGA monitor. It uses the Tiny VGA PMOD pinout and a 25.175 MHz clock, and is intended to be run on the Tiny Tapeout demo board with both PMODs attached. After reset, pressing a gamepad button causes its corresponding symbol to appear on screen. It is a demonstration of combining the Gamepad and Tiny VGA PMODs, derived from the VGA Playground, and needs both external PMOD boards to operate.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gcd_stephan.summary: This module computes the greatest common divisor of two 15-bit integers, taking the operands across the eight ui and eight uio input pins and returning a 7-bit result on the output pins. A request signal on uio[7] indicates when operands have been presented, and an acknowledge signal on uo[7] indicates when the first operand has been received and when the GCD is ready. The documented test procedure is to hold the first operand, raise request, wait for acknowledge, then present the second operand and read the result. It is a small single-tile Verilog design that expects buttons and LEDs as external hardware, and the documentation gives no details of the internal algorithm.
ttihp25a/tt_um_gcd_stephan.review_notes: Removed alu and synchronizer tags because the source describes a GCD module with a request/acknowledge handshake, not an ALU or clock-domain synchronizer.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gfcwfzkm_scope_bfh_mht1_3.summary: This design implements a basic oscilloscope and signal generator on an ASIC, using an external ADC, DAC, FRAM, and HDMI Pmod. It samples input signals, buffers them in FRAM, and displays waveforms on an HDMI screen, with the display rotated 90 degrees due to memory constraints. The signal generator uses direct digital synthesis to produce sine, square, triangle, and sawtooth waves, and the oscilloscope supports trigger functionality. The design requires multiple external Pmods and outputs settings via UART.
ttihp25a/tt_um_gfcwfzkm_scope_bfh_mht1_3.review_notes: Removed nco (DDS, not NCO) and added pmod, button, dip-switch, and oscilloscope.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gfg_development_tinymande.summary: This design generates a Mandelbrot set image and outputs it via a VGA driver, using an external RP2040 to emulate a framebuffer. It includes a serial interface for configuration and control, and the VGA output follows the Tiny VGA pinout. The design requires a Tiny VGA PMOD for display and an RP2040 for framebuffer emulation. The documentation is brief and lacks details on the serial protocol and exact operation, but the core function is clear.
ttihp25a/tt_um_gfg_development_tinymande.review_notes: Removed vga: VGA is only described as an optional output mode for the Mandelbrot image generator.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gmejiamtz.summary: This project implements a small Configurable Logic Block (CLB) with a 3-input Look-Up Table (LUT3). It takes two 8-bit inputs: one for the LUT configuration and control signals, and another for the boolean function arguments. The output is the evaluation of the configured boolean function. The design can be tested by setting the LUT to implement a NAND3 function and using switches and LEDs for input and output.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gregac_tiny_nn.summary: This is a toy neural network accelerator aimed at convolutional neural networks, containing 16-bit floating point add and multiply units using an approximation of the BF16 encoding. It supports a 4x2 convolution operation with streamed image pixels and an accumulate operation with optional bias and ReLU, all controlled by operation codes sent over a 16-bit input formed from ui_in and uio_in. Results are emitted as 16-bit values split over two clock cycles on the 8-bit output, so the user must know which cycles carry valid data. The Verilog is generated from a separate SystemVerilog repository that holds the full verification environment and software, both described as work in progress at tapeout time, and no specific external hardware is required beyond something to drive the sequences, such as the demo board's RP2040.
ttihp25a/tt_um_gregac_tiny_nn.review_notes: Removed dsp and image-processing as unsupported; added tpu and mac-unit which the CNN accelerator description supports.

ttihp25a/tt_um_gus16.summary: This project is a 16-bit experimental CPU called GUS16 with a serial port, PWM output, general purpose I/O and an external memory interface, with memory provided off-chip. It includes a bootloader that loads programs over the serial port, and the documented basic test is to connect at 115200 baud, 8N1, and send an 'L', which should be echoed back.
